dialog.body: Zoning and Inspections, this is Greg.
[whispering] Hi, good afternoon. I'm sorry, I'm going to be whispering the whole time. My little one is napping right in the next room and if she wakes up, that's the end of this call.
No problem, I can hear you fine. Go ahead, what do you need?

My name is Lidia Gomes. I own a small shop, and I want to put a sandwich board out on the sidewalk in front. I called the main line Tuesday and they told me it's a sign permit, which, fine. But nobody could tell me how big the board is allowed to be. I was passed around twice and then I got a voicemail box.
Yeah, that happens. Sandwich boards are handled as a sign permit here, so you're in the right department. Let me pull up what we've got on the A-frame signs.
Thank you. I wrote down my questions so I don't forget any, because honestly I've been on the phone a lot this week about this.

Smart. Okay, so the size. There's a maximum height and width for a sidewalk sandwich board, and it's measured on the board itself, not including anything you hang on it. Do you have the dimensions of the one you want to buy?
I do. It's two feet wide and three feet six inches tall. I measured the one I'm looking at online. It's a chalkboard style with a wooden frame.
Hang on one second, let me look at the sign section to make sure I read you the right numbers.
[whispering] Of course. Take your time, she's out cold.

[pause] Okay. I'm looking at it. Generally those A-frames are limited to about two feet by three feet, give or take, and the board has to be the sort that sits on its own, no anchoring to the sidewalk. Yours is a few inches over on the height from what you're telling me.
A few inches over. So that's not allowed? Because I'll be honest, that's irritating. Nobody at the main number mentioned there was a limit at all, and I was about to order it.

I'd hold off on ordering. The size limit is the thing people trip on. If you go with two by three, you're fine on that part. If you want the taller one, you'd have to ask about a variance, and that's a longer process for a chalkboard.
No, I don't want a long process. I'll find a smaller one. Let me write that down. Two feet by three feet. Is that measured with the legs open or folded?
Open, the way it stands on the sidewalk. That's the footprint people actually see.
Open. Okay. And is there anything about how far into the sidewalk it can sit? My shop is on a narrow stretch.
There is. You have to leave a clear walking path past it, so people with strollers or wheelchairs can get by. And it has to come in every night when you close. It can't be left out overnight.
Fine. In at close. Clear path. I'm writing all this down. Now, the part I really need. What documents do I bring? I'd like to do this in one trip, if possible.

Good plan. You'll fill out the sign permit application, and we have that here at the counter or you can pick it up. Bring a picture or a drawing of the sign with the dimensions on it. A product page printout works fine.
A printout of the product page, with the measurements. Okay.
Then a simple sketch or description of where on the sidewalk it'll sit, in front of which door, how far from the curb. If you're leasing, bring something from your landlord saying it's okay.
I do lease. Do I need a letter, or will an email do?
A signed letter is cleaner. An email printed out has worked for some people, but I'd go with the letter if you can get one.
A signed letter. Alright. Anything else? Proof of insurance? A business license?

Bring your business registration or license if you have it. On the insurance, since it's going on a public sidewalk, they may ask for a certificate showing liability coverage. I'd bring a copy so you don't have to come back.
Okay. So that's the application, product printout with measurements, a sketch of the placement, landlord letter, business license, and the insurance certificate. Did I get all of it?
That's it. You nailed it.
[whispering] Good. And is there a fee? I don't want to show up and be surprised.
There is a fee for the permit, yes. I don't have the exact amount in front of me for that type, so the counter will tell you when you come in. Bring a check or card to be safe.
Hm. That's the second person this week who couldn't give me a number. But all right. What are the counter hours? I can only come when my husband is home to watch her.
We're open weekdays during regular business hours, the office closes late afternoon. It's almost four now, so you've missed today. Tomorrow morning would work, or any weekday next week.
Tomorrow is Friday. He's home Friday. I'll try for the morning. Do I need an appointment?
No appointment. Walk up to the counter and say you're there for a sign permit. Somebody will take you.
And how long does it take to get it? Do I walk out with it or wait?
For a basic sandwich board, if the paperwork is complete, it's often handled quickly. If something's missing, it goes in review and that takes longer. That's why I'd bring everything.
Which is exactly why I called ahead. I don't want to take a morning off and be told I'm missing a piece of paper.
Understood. If you want, I can put a note on the file with your name that you called and what you were told. If you get someone else at the counter, they'll see it.
Yes, please do that. That would help. Lidia Gomes, G-O-M-E-S.
Got it. Gomes with an S. And what's the name of the shop?
I'd rather not go into that on the phone. The name will be on the application. Just the note with my name is fine.
That works. Do you want to leave a callback number in case I need to reach you?
Yes. It's 401-555-0191. Please call only if you have to, though. If it rings while she's sleeping, I'll have to let it go to voicemail.
Okay, 401-555-0191. I'll only use it if something changes on the size rules. Anything else I can help with?
Just to confirm. Two by three, open, no anchoring, in every night, clear path, and bring the six items. Correct?
Correct on all of it.
Thank you, Greg. I appreciate you actually answering the question. I'll see you tomorrow, hopefully before ten.
Sounds good. Have a good one, and good luck with the nap.
[whispering] Thanks. Goodbye.
